newsitem.title: FRANCE: French judge to probe Elf German deal.
newsitem.headline: French judge to probe Elf German deal.

text.p: A French magistrate investigating alleged corruption by former executives of the Elf Aquitaine oil company has been authorised to extend her probe to suspect payments involving Germany, justice sources said on Tuesday.

The public prosecutor's office on Monday gave judge Eva Joly permission to investigate alleged covert commission paid in 1992 in connection with Elf's purchase of the former East German petrochemicals combine Leuna and the Minol petrol station network, the sources said.
Both were acquired from a German government agency (Treuhandanstalt) in charge of privatising the former communist state's industries.
The investigation concerns suspected misuse of corporate funds.

The newspaper Le Parisien said Elf paid a 13.5 million mark commission linked to the Leuna deal to a Liechtenstein-based company -- Noblepac -- owned by Andre Guelfi, an intermediary who is already under judicial investigation in the case.
The magistrate wanted to trace the recipients of the money, Le Parisien said.
A spokesman for Elf declined comment on the report. He said a new refinery the company was building at Leuna, near Leipzig, as part of the deal, would be operational later this year.

The Elf case began as an investigation of alleged financial irregularities when Loik Le Floch-Prigent was chairman in 1988-93. It has since widened to cover Elf's operations and commission payments abroad, including dealings in Gabon and Venezuela.
